title: [design] dao_origin pin table keyed by IID is unimplementable post-AddrForKey (validator can't reverse address→IID)
description: Surfaced by the Python AddrForKey migration (7pt2). python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_origin.py:327 does source_iid = source_address.packed[8:16] then pin_table.pinned_pubkey_for(source_iid). Pre-migration the routable address's lower 64 bits WERE the SHA-512 IID, so this recovered the IID from the wire address. Post-migration (upstream AddrForKey) address[8:16] is a bit-packed fragment of the inverted key, NOT the IID, so the lookup misses (ORIGIN_NOT_PINNED) even for correctly-pinned origins. The DAO origin validator receives only the source address on the wire and cannot derive the SHA-512 IID from it — the IID-embedding shortcut is gone. DESIGN DECISION NEEDED (same class as 5muj route_hash): (a) re-key PinTable by full 16-byte source address (lookup = yggdrasil_address(pubkey) == source, iterate or index by address); (b) key PinTable by addr[8:16] explicitly as a documented 64-bit address-tag (weaker collision profile than IID); or (c) carry the origin IID explicitly in the DAO. Affects Python dao_origin.py, the PinTable protocol, and the C/Rust DAO-origin equivalents. Failing Python tests blocked on this: tests/rpl/test_dao_prefix_authorization.py (6 tests) and any dao_origin validator path that pins by IID. See also 5muj (route_hash) — likely the same decision.
